skills.body:
---
name: design-space-explore
description: "Generates a batch of CAD variants directly in Autodesk Fusion by applying changed parameters to an engineer's existing model, never designing from scratch and never overwriting the base. Checks first whether the parameters the engineer wants to vary actually drive the model's geometry, and stops rather than generating garbage if they don't. Confirms the variant count with the engineer before generating anything. Captures mass, volume, bounding box and every other model-computed property per variant, and hands the batch off in the shape trade-study-report consumes — it does not run analysis itself. Use when someone says \"explore the design space,\" \"generate variants,\" \"try different wall thicknesses,\" \"run a parameter sweep,\" or \"vary this and see what happens.\""
compatibility: "Requires Autodesk Fusion (desktop, with the document open). There is no other CAD backend and no file-only path — without Fusion connected, the skill reports exactly what is needed rather than running degraded. Never overwrites the base model."
---

# Design Space Explore

An engineering team designing a part rarely has one answer. They have a
**design space** — a range of possible designs bounded by what they're
allowed to vary (wall thickness, rib count, hole pattern, material) and what
the part must satisfy (envelope, mass, load, cost, manufacturability).
Modeling one design at a time, by hand, means evaluating three to five
options and picking the best of a small set. This skill generates many at
once, directly in the CAD tool the engineer already has open.

**It does not design from scratch.** It takes a model the engineer already
has and generates variants of it — that constraint is what makes the output
trustworthy and reviewable rather than a pile of new geometry nobody asked
for.

**It does not run analysis.** It produces the variants and the manifest
describing them, so an analysis tool or a person evaluates each one and
returns results, which `trade-study-report` then consumes.

**Quick start**

```
→ Connect: Fusion, with the base model open in the desktop app
→ Read the model's parameter set. Not driving what was asked? Stop and say so
→ Confirm the variant plan — parameters, ranges, step, and the resulting count
→ Generate. Verify each regenerated; failures at range extremes are expected
→ Capture per-variant properties: parameter values, mass, volume, bounding box
→ Produce the manifest in the shape trade-study-report consumes
→ Never touch the base model. Variants are new documents, clearly named
```

---

## Inputs

| Input | Source | Form |
|---|---|---|
| The base model | Fusion (open desktop document) | Live CAD connection |
| Parameters to vary, with ranges | Engineer, in conversation | Conversation |
| Constraints | Engineer, in conversation, and the trade study definition | Conversation / document |
| Trade study targets and criteria | `trade-study-report` definition, or a document in M365 | Document |
| Prior variants and results | M365 | Documents |

---

## Workflow

### Step 1 — Connect to the CAD environment

One implementation, Fusion, behind one interface. Read
`reference/cad-adapter.md` for the interface and the connector behaviors that
break a naive script.

- **Fusion** — desktop only, and acts on the open document via command-based
  operations on live geometry. There is no server-side fetch path; if the
  document is not open on the user's machine, there is nothing to act on.

Record the backend as `cad_backend` on the manifest, so a second CAD
connector drops in later without a contract change.

### Step 2 — Read the parameter set, and check what actually drives it

**This check comes first, before anything else, and it is the single
biggest practical risk in the skill.** A parametric model is built from
driving dimensions — change `wall_thickness` and the geometry regenerates.
Many real production models are not properly parametric, and automated
variant generation on one that isn't will not work.

Read the model's parameters and report which ones are actually driving
geometry. **Where a parameter the engineer wants to vary is not a driving
dimension, stop and say so** rather than generating variants that silently
ignore it. Read `reference/parametric-check.md`.

### Step 3 — Confirm the variant plan

Before generating anything: which parameters, which ranges, which step or
sampling strategy, and **the resulting variant count, stated plainly.**

**Generating 200 variants nobody asked for is the obvious failure.** Five
parameters at five values each is 3,125 combinations — show the count and
get an explicit yes before the batch runs. Read
`reference/variant-generation.md`.

### Step 4 — Generate, and verify each one

Apply each confirmed parameter set to the existing model. After each,
verify the model regenerated without error. The open, save-as-new, apply and
untouched-check sequence is `reference/adapt-prior-model.md` — the same
mechanism `rfq-to-quote` uses to adapt a prior part's model.

**A failed regeneration is expected, not a bug** — geometry that
self-intersects or a feature that fails to rebuild at a range extreme
happens routinely and does not abort the batch. Report it per variant, with
what failed.

### Step 5 — Capture per-variant properties

Parameter values, mass, volume, bounding box, and any other property the
model computed.

**A property the model could not compute is absent, not zero.** A variant
with no mass reading is unmeasured, not massless, and reporting it as zero
would win a lower-is-better weight criterion outright.

### Step 6 — Produce the handoff manifest

One row per variant — its ID, its parameter values, its computed
properties, its status, and its document reference — per
`../../shared/contracts/variant-manifest.md`, in exactly the shape
`trade-study-report` consumes.

**A failed or skipped variant stays in the manifest, never dropped.** A
dropped row is indistinguishable from a variant nobody considered, and the
trade study would then report a design space narrower than the one actually
explored.

### Step 7 — Never touch the base model

Variants are new documents, or clearly-named configurations of the base —
never a modification in place. State what was created, and where.

---

## Approval gates

**Nothing generates without the variant plan being confirmed** — parameters,
ranges, and the resulting count, agreed before the batch runs. This is the
skill's one real chance to prevent a runaway job; a live CAD connection
generates 3,000 low-value variants exactly as easily as 30 good ones.

**The base model is never modified.** Every variant is a new document or a
clearly-named configuration, so there is nothing to approve or roll back on
the original.

This skill does not run analysis and does not decide anything about the
trade study — it hands the manifest off. `trade-study-report` and the
engineer own what happens next.

---

## Output

**Every document this skill produces is printed in the reply, in full.**
Saving a copy to a file as well is fine, as Word or Excel per `../../shared/replies.md`, never `.txt`; a file *instead of* the reply is not.
The person reads the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives
in it — a document only on disk has been neither seen nor checked.
**A record handed to another skill is saved and summarised, never pasted as
raw YAML**; memory blocks are written where the plant's memory lives; and the
name on an approval is asked, never taken from the account. All three per
`../../shared/replies.md`.

**The generated variants**, in the CAD system, consistently named and
traceable back to their parameter set.

**The variant manifest** — per
`../../shared/contracts/variant-manifest.md`: the parameters varied, the
parametric check result, and per variant its ID, parameter values, computed
properties, status, and document reference.

**The generation report** — what succeeded, what failed to regenerate and
why, what was skipped and why. Rendered in the house artifact style
(`../../shared/artifact-style.md`) when there is enough of a batch to be
worth referring back to.

**The handoff package** — the manifest plus the generation report, ready for
an analysis tool or a person to evaluate and return results into, which
`trade-study-report` then consumes.

---

## Edge cases and failure modes

- **The base model isn't properly parametric** — the most likely real-world
  blocker. Detect and report before generating anything.
- **Fusion isn't open, or the customer uses Fusion's web client** — the
  connector cannot work at all. Detect and say so plainly; there is no
  server-side fetch path.
- **The connector replays an earlier script** — geometry nobody asked for
  appears, or read-only calls fail with "cannot modify." Stop and ask the user
  to restart Fusion; see `reference/cad-adapter.md`.
- **Geometry fails to regenerate at a range extreme** — expected. Report it
  per variant; do not abort the batch.
- **The parameter combination count explodes** — five parameters at five
  values is 3,125. Always show the count and confirm before generating.
- **The model has external references or in-context relationships** —
  variant generation can break them. Detect and warn before generating.
- **CAD operations are slow** — this is a long-running batch, not a single
  blocking call. Design for progress reporting, not silence until it
  finishes.

---

## Degradation

**One CAD tool, on one platform.** The skill works for customers running
Fusion on the desktop, with no cloud path. There is no fallback CAD backend —
no connector currently reaches SolidWorks, Creo, NX or Inventor, so a customer
on any of those has no path to this skill at all. State that plainly rather
than letting a prospect discover it for the first time in a demo. Keep the
CAD-adapter layer regardless, so a CAD connector appearing later drops in
without a redesign.

**If Fusion is not available** — the skill cannot generate variants and says
so, naming exactly what is needed: Fusion desktop with the document open.
`trade-study-report` is unaffected — its manifest can be hand-authored by an
engineer with no CAD backend at all, per its own contract.

---

## Chain position

Not part of a named chain, but feeds `trade-study-report` directly — the
same producer-consumer relationship `breakdown-diagnosis` has with
`daily-production-report` in Chain 4.

**Metric.** Configurations evaluated per program; design cycle time.

---

## Reference files

| File | Load when |
|---|---|
| `reference/cad-adapter.md` | Step 1 — the backend behind the interface, and the connector behaviors to read before the first call |
| `reference/parametric-check.md` | Step 2 — always, before generating anything |
| `reference/variant-generation.md` | Steps 3 to 7 — confirming the plan, generating, and the manifest |
| `reference/adapt-prior-model.md` | Steps 4 and 7 — open the base, save as new, apply, confirm the base is untouched |
| `../../shared/contracts/variant-manifest.md` | On emit — the exact shape `trade-study-report` consumes |

Use when someone says \"run the CAPA chain,\" \"take this nonconformance through to an 8D,\" \"inspection to CAPA,\" or asks for the full corrective-action workflow."
compatibility: "Requires none. Chains ncr-writeup and root-cause-capa. Reads Microsoft 365 and the ERP (Oracle NetSuite or Infor M3) where connected; runs on pasted findings and file exports with no connector. Never asserts a requirement it cannot locate, never correlates across clocks it could not align, and nothing customer-facing leaves without review of the redaction diff."
---

# Inspection to CAPA

Chain 2. `ncr-writeup` → `root-cause-capa`.

The path from "we found a bad part" to "we fixed the reason, and we can prove
it." It ends on the 8D and its redacted customer pack.

**Quick start**

```
→ Write the NCR against a CITED requirement. Cannot find one? Block. Never invent
→ Search history AT CREATION, not on request. Did the earlier fix hold?
→ Gate 1: the quality owner confirms the NCR and its containment
→ Verify the clocks BEFORE correlating. Misaligned? Refuse, and say what survives
→ Ranked candidate chains with evidence FOR and AGAINST. Never one verdict
→ 8D: D1-D5 and D7 populated. D6 and D8 stay empty placeholders
→ Gate 2: nothing customer-facing leaves without the redaction diff reviewed
```

---

## Inputs

| Input | Source | Form |
|---|---|---|
| The finding | Inspector notes, an inspection export, an operator report, a customer complaint | Conversation, M365, pasted |
| Everything else | Whatever the two member skills read | See each skill |

---

## The seven steps

**1. An inspection result or a suspect lot starts it.**

**2. Write the nonconformance** against the requirement, with quantity and
location. All five containment locations are addressed, including with a zero
quantity, because an omitted location reads as "none there" rather than "not
checked."

**Gate 1** — the quality owner confirms the NCR and the containment plan.
**This is a pause, and the chain says so:** *"Paused at Gate 1, after step 2.
The NCR is a draft. A quality owner confirms four things before step 4 — the
finding, the cited requirement, the suspect scope, and the containment plan."*
A missing citation is one reason the NCR is not ready; it is not the gate.
Fixing the citation does not unblock the chain — the owner's confirmation does.
The history search in step 3 still runs at write time, because it belongs to
the NCR. Per `../../shared/approval-gates.md`.

**3. Search history for the same problem.** This runs automatically at write
time, not on request, because the moment of detection is the only moment anyone
is looking.

**Whether the earlier fix held is the highest-value single line in this
chain.** A recurrence after a *closed* CAPA is a materially different finding
from a first occurrence, and it changes what happens next. Surface it as such.

**4. Read the prior tickets, inspection data and production history together**,
aligned onto one zone-aware timeline. Verify the clocks first; where alignment
cannot be verified, refuse to correlate and say which conclusions survive
anyway.

**5. Propose ranked candidate causal chains**, each stated as a chain with
supporting *and contradicting* evidence attached to each link, and the cheapest
test that would confirm or kill it. Never one confident verdict: a confident
wrong root cause closes the investigation and the fix fails.

**6. Draft the 8D.** D1 to D5 and D7 populated from the evidence. D6 and D8
stay as structured placeholders, because they need a real-world outcome and a
human signature.

**7. Produce the customer-facing pack with a redaction pass.** **Gate 2.**

---

## Approval gates

| Gate | Where | What it protects |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | After step 2 | The quality owner confirms the finding, the cited requirement, the suspect scope and the containment plan |
| 2 | After step 7 | Nothing customer-facing leaves without review of the **redaction diff** |

The redaction pass is a reviewable diff, never a silent filter. The internal 8D
carries cost data, other customers' names, supplier identity and internal
process detail; the customer version must not. **A recurrence stays in** —
removing it is misrepresentation, not redaction.

---

## Output

**Every document this skill produces is printed in the reply, in full.**
Saving a copy to a file as well is fine, as Word or Excel per `../../shared/replies.md`, never `.txt`; a file *instead of* the reply is not.
The person reads the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives
in it — a document only on disk has been neither seen nor checked.
**A record handed to another skill is saved and summarised, never pasted as
raw YAML**; memory blocks are written where the plant's memory lives; and the
name on an approval is asked, never taken from the account. All three per
`../../shared/replies.md`.

The NCR in the plant's controlled template, the containment plan ordered by
urgency, the recurrence finding with whether the previous fix held, the ranked
candidate causes with their discriminating tests, the drafted 8D, the evidence
appendix, and the redacted customer pack.

**The figures block** — required, inside the evidence appendix. Every
measurement, control limit, ratio and count the chain states is printed from
the computation and listed with it, and the prose quotes the block. Two member
skills doing the same arithmetic must not arrive at two different multiples of
the same limit. Per `../../shared/computed-figures.md`.

Where the leading candidate points at purchased material, the **supplier-caused
flag** is raised, which is the trigger into Chain 5. See
`supplier-escape-to-alternate-source`.

**The Quality command-center page: the Quality Register** — open corrective
actions, carrying the NCR and the 8D by reference, updated in place per
`../../shared/live-dashboard.md`. **The chain writes no register row of its
own.** `ncr-writeup` writes the row at step 2 and `root-cause-capa` adds the
8D fields at step 6, both keyed `<site>_<ncr_ref>`, so one chain run leaves
one row. The chain reports the register once, at the end: the dashboard line
with its URL and the sensitivity line, or the fallback with *"The Quality
Register was not updated: [reason]."* It is reported as updated only when a
publish returned a URL in this run, and never as shared. Read
`../../shared/command-center.md`.

---

## Edge cases and failure modes

- **The requirement cannot be located** — the chain **blocks at step 2**. Never
  invent one. That is a complete and honest outcome.
- **Traceability is incomplete** — the suspect scope **widens** and says why.
  Never narrow it to make the number look better.
- **The clocks cannot be aligned** — step 4 refuses to correlate. Non
  time-dependent analysis still runs, and the output says which is which.
- **Two candidates are supported equally** — present both. A stated tie is a
  real finding, and it names the test that would settle it.
- **No prior history exists** — say so. Absence of recurrence is not evidence
  of a one-off.

---

## Degradation

| Not available | What happens |
|---|---|
| The quality document library | Report "no searchable history available" at step 3. **Never silence**, which reads as "no recurrence" |
| The sensor export, or it misses the event window | Say so. Do not reason from adjacent data as if it were the event |
| The plant's 8D template | Use the standard eight-discipline structure and flag that the controlled template was unavailable |
| A CMMS connector (Limble or any other) | See below |

**Check the freshness of every export before correlating on it.** A scheduled
export that silently stopped produces a timeline with a hole in it, and the
hole looks like an absence of evidence rather than an absence of data. State
the coverage window of each source in the evidence appendix.

**If Limble isn't included, or no CMMS connector is live** — minor here. Maintenance history arrives in the
same scheduled export as everything else and the maintenance-correlation check
runs on it unchanged. What changes is freshness: name maintenance explicitly as
an export-sourced input in the evidence appendix rather than letting it read as
live, since a repair logged after the last export will not be on the timeline
at all.

---

## Chain position

**This is Chain 2 itself.** Members: `ncr-writeup`, `root-cause-capa`.

**Metric.** CAPA closure time and first-pass yield, both owned by
`root-cause-capa`. `ncr-writeup` also moves nonconformance closure time and
escape response time inside this chain; the chain does not claim them, because
it is named for the corrective-action loop.

---

## Reference files

| File | Load when |
|---|---|
| `../ncr-writeup/SKILL.md` | Steps 2 and 3 |
| `../root-cause-capa/SKILL.md` | Steps 4 to 7 |
| `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md` | The handoff, and what blocks `root-cause-capa` |
| `../../shared/command-center.md` | The Quality page, and when "updated" may be said |
| `../../shared/live-dashboard.md` | The Quality Register: one row per NCR, the banner, the fallback |
| `../../shared/computed-figures.md` | Before stating any figure — the figures block |
| `../../shared/approval-gates.md` | At both gates — a gate is a pause, and how to say where the chain stopped |

skills.body:
---
name: morning-plant-pulse
description: "Runs the overnight chain that has the morning production report waiting before anyone asks for it: joins last night's planning, production and maintenance exports, flags the mismatched keys, then computes output against plan, OEE with its three components, downtime ranked two ways, priced losses and the exceptions needing a decision. Stores a record per production day and keeps one Operations Command Center dashboard per site up to date, with a 14 and 30 day trend. Safe to run unattended. Use when someone says \"run the morning pulse,\" \"do the overnight report,\" \"morning plant pulse,\" \"update the operations dashboard,\" or schedules the daily production run."
compatibility: "Requires none. Chains data-consolidate and daily-production-report, then publishes the site's Operations Command Center dashboard to the Claude artifact store where the artifact tools exist, else offers the page in the conversation. Reads M365 exports, NetSuite or Infor M3, and a CMMS connector where connected; runs on the export folder alone. Writes to no system of record, so it is safe to schedule. Asks nothing, is idempotent, reports its own gaps."
---

# Morning Plant Pulse

Chain 3. `data-consolidate` → `daily-production-report` → publish.

**The only scheduled chain, and the only one with no approval gate.** Those two
facts are the same fact: it reads, it produces a page, and it writes to no
system of record. The dashboard it publishes lives in the user's own Claude
artifact store, which is not a system of record either. That is precisely why
it is safe to run unattended, and why no other chain in this build should ever
be scheduled.

The page is rebuilt overnight so it exists before the morning meeting. A
supervisor otherwise spends sixty to ninety minutes assembling it by hand out
of the same four or five exports. **The first run creates one dashboard per
site; every later run updates that same dashboard**, so nobody has to save
over yesterday's page.

**Quick start**

```
→ Join last night's exports; flag mismatched keys by class
→ Compute output vs plan, OEE with its three components shown separately
→ Downtime ranked BOTH ways: by minutes and by frequency
→ Price the losses. Week-over-week movers come from the stored day records
→ Write the day record, keyed <site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>. Missing export? data_complete: false
→ Find the dashboard: stored URL, then exact title. Neither? Create it
→ Say "updated" ONLY when the publish returned a URL in this run
→ Can't publish? Page saved to pulse-output/ + "the dashboard was not updated"
→ Reply: ~150-word summary naming the page; full page in the reply only if nothing could be written
→ Export did not land? STILL RUN. Gap at the top, gap in the trend, never a zero
→ Ask nothing. There is nobody there at 4am
→ Idempotent: a re-run overwrites that day's record on the same dashboard
```

---

## Inputs

**First, find the plant setup:** from the task's own folder (never `cd` into the plugin), run
`python3 -I <this skill's folder>/../../shared/scripts/plant_setup.py find`, do its `setup_page_first` step, then read the profile at
`profile_path` and any rate at `rates_path`, per `../../shared/replies.md`.

| Input | Source | Form |
|---|---|---|
| Planning, production and maintenance exports | The M365 export folder | CSV/XLSX |
| Standard cost, open work orders | The ERP (NetSuite or Infor M3) | Connector |
| Maintenance work orders in progress | CMMS | CMMS connector, else the maintenance export |
| Stored day records, for the trend and week-over-week | The dashboard's own `pulse_days` collection | `ArtifactData` `query`, per `../../shared/contracts/pulse-day-record.md` |
| The dashboard's URL | The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page, then an exact-title lookup | Open work page, `Artifact` `list` |
| Source clocks, shift pattern, day boundary | `## Plant context` | Config |

---

## The three steps

**First, run the compute engine.** Steps 1 and 2 are done in code that ships
with this skill, so every run computes the same numbers the same way:

```
python3 -I <this skill's folder>/scripts/pulse_compute.py --exports <export folder> \
  --out pulse-output [--day YYYY-MM-DD] [--profile <profile_path>] [--rates <rates_path>]
```

It applies the ladder, the eight classes and the integrity flags of
`data-consolidate`, and the OEE, ranking, pricing and exception rules of
`daily-production-report`, and writes `figures.csv` (the figures block, one row
per number with its filter), `pulse_model.json` (everything the page shows,
already computed) and `day_records.json` (one day record per covered day).
**Build the page from `pulse_model.json` and quote `figures.csv`. Never
recompute, retype or round a number it holds.** The judgment stays yours: the
wording, which exceptions are significant, the reschedule move, the publish.
What each key holds is `reference/compute-engine.md`. **If the engine cannot
run** (no code execution) **or exits non-zero**, do steps 1 and 2 as written
below and say which happened; never mix the two.

**1. Join the exports** through `data-consolidate`, on the records the plant
already has, with mismatched keys flagged by class.

**2. Compute the report** through `daily-production-report`: output against
plan, equipment losses ranked by minutes and by frequency, priced in dollars,
and the exceptions that need a decision today. **Week-over-week movers come
from the stored day records**, read at the start of step 3 before the page is
built, never from a prior page. The pulse hands that history to step 6 of
`daily-production-report`.

**3. Publish the dashboard.** Per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`, which names
every tool call. In order:

1. **Find the dashboard.** The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page first; then
   `Artifact` `list` for the exact title *"<Site>: Operations Command
   Center"*; only when both find nothing does this run create it. A scheduled
   run starts with no memory of earlier runs, so it looks every time.
2. **Build the day record** for the production day, every field, per
   `../../shared/contracts/pulse-day-record.md`, keyed `<site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>`.
   A missing export makes it `data_complete: false` with the gap named. Its
   metrics are null, never zero.
3. **Existing dashboard:** `read` it, `query` `pulse_days`, `set` the day
   record, compute the trend from the stored records in code, then publish to
   the same `url`. **First run:** back-fill (below), publish with
   `capabilities: {db: {}}` and the fixed title, `batch` the records against
   the new URL, write the URL to the `## Dashboards` line on the Open work
   page, then `open` the dashboard so it is what the person sees.
4. **Render the short Operations page,** after the publish so it can link
   to the dashboard: `python3 -I <this skill's folder>/scripts/render_short.py
   --out pulse-output [--full-page-url <url>]`. It writes
   `operations-short-<site>-<day>.html` beside the figures and checks itself;
   on a failed check it writes nothing, and the reply says so. It is a
   separate page from the dashboard and never replaces it. Per
   `reference/short-page.md`.
5. **Report it,** as the last line of the run: *"Updated **Fairview:
   Operations Command Center**, `<url>`. Private to you until you share it."*
   Or the fallback: the page saved as
   `pulse-output/operations-<site>-<day>.html` (in the reply only when no
   file can be written), its placement line, and
   *"The dashboard was not updated: [reason]."*

**Say "updated" only when the publish returned a URL in this run.** Never
"shared," never "scheduled," never "posted." The dashboard is private until
the user shares it, and the pulse never shares it. A run that says "updated"
without a URL from this run has told the meeting to trust a page nobody
rebuilt.

**Only the pulse publishes the Operations dashboard.** `daily-production-report`
run alone, and Chain 4, keep offering their page in the conversation. Two
dashboards showing the same numbers is how a meeting ends up arguing about
which one is right.

**Back-fill on the first run only.** When the exports cover several production
days, the run that creates the dashboard writes a record for every day the
planning, production and downtime exports fully cover, so the trend opens with
history. A day they only partly cover is written `data_complete: false`, so it
shows as a gap rather than as a bad day. Later runs write their own day.

What the page holds, panel by panel, is `reference/operations-dashboard.md`.

---

## What "safe to run unattended" actually requires

Three properties. Each is a real constraint, not a nicety.

**It asks nobody anything.** There is no one at 4am to answer. Where an
attended run would ask which date range or which of several exports to use, the
unattended run takes the production-day range from the `## Plant context` block
and **says which it used**. **With no Plant context at all**, it uses the latest
complete production day present in the exports, says so in the freshness
banner, and lists *no plant profile* among the gaps. It never blocks on the
missing profile, and never picks today's date, which has no data. A run that blocks on a question produces nothing,
and nothing is worse than a partial report, because the gap is only discovered
at the meeting. The publish step asks nothing either: where two artifacts carry
the exact title, it uses the stored URL's, or the most recently updated, and
names both.

**Asking nobody does not mean deciding for them.** Where plan and output spell
a part differently, the unattended run neither drops the row nor joins it
silently. It shows the variance **labelled provisional**, shows both spellings
verbatim, and lists each normalization it relied on as **proposed, awaiting
approval**, for whoever reads the page to accept or reject. Normalizations on
the profile's `### Approved normalizations` list are used as they stand; each
overnight run rebuilds the dataset, so that list is what carries a yes from one
night to the next. This is
not a gate — nothing is applied and nothing is written — and the rule is
`../../shared/approval-gates.md`, *When nobody is there to ask*.

**A list of data problems holds problems, and it is built by class number.**
Take the classified mismatches from step 1 and route each class before any
row is numbered:

| Class | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| 1 orphan, 2 format drift, 3 leading zeros, 4 revision suffix, 5 case and whitespace, 8 duplicate key | The numbered **Data problems** table, and its count |
| 7 date window | The coverage line in the freshness banner. Not a numbered row |
| 6 genuine one-sided record | **"Checked, nothing wrong"**, a separate block after the table. Never a row number, never in the count |
| 6 with `contradicted_by` set | The numbered **Data problems** table, as *one-sided, contradicted by* the named record, and its count. Never "Checked, nothing wrong" |

A record decides its class from its own type and dates, never from a part
number someone recognises. A Class 6 record that appears in the table *and*
in the recap has still been counted as a problem; it appears in the recap
only. **A duplicate key is counted by the rows that collide at the tab's
grain, from the query** (work order, shift and production day): if WO-88201
has three rows, and two of them (509 and 480 good, both 07:00)
are the duplicate; the 95 on the 23:00 shift is its own shift. Say both
numbers, and the figures block shows the filter. And a downtime record
from `breakdown-diagnosis` with no `safety_flagged` is **blocked**: listed

until the user shares it. The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page is

unless `saved` returned ok in this run. The `## Plant context` block is never touched by

execute unattended; the host provides the trigger. Read

# Morning Plant Pulse

Chain 3. `data-consolidate` → `daily-production-report` → publish.

**The only scheduled chain, and the only one with no approval gate.** Those two
facts are the same fact: it reads, it produces a page, and it writes to no
system of record. The dashboard it publishes lives in the user's own Claude
artifact store, which is not a system of record either. That is precisely why
it is safe to run unattended, and why no other chain in this build should ever
be scheduled.

The page is rebuilt overnight so it exists before the morning meeting. A
supervisor otherwise spends sixty to ninety minutes assembling it by hand out
of the same four or five exports. **The first run creates one dashboard per
site; every later run updates that same dashboard**, so nobody has to save
over yesterday's page.

**Quick start**

```
→ Join last night's exports; flag mismatched keys by class
→ Compute output vs plan, OEE with its three components shown separately
→ Downtime ranked BOTH ways: by minutes and by frequency
→ Price the losses. Week-over-week movers come from the stored day records
→ Write the day record, keyed <site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>. Missing export? data_complete: false
→ Find the dashboard: stored URL, then exact title. Neither? Create it
→ Say "updated" ONLY when the publish returned a URL in this run
→ Can't publish? Page saved to pulse-output/ + "the dashboard was not updated"
→ Reply: ~150-word summary naming the page; full page in the reply only if nothing could be written
→ Export did not land? STILL RUN. Gap at the top, gap in the trend, never a zero
→ Ask nothing. There is nobody there at 4am
→ Idempotent: a re-run overwrites that day's record on the same dashboard
```

---

## Inputs

**First, find the plant setup:** from the task's own folder (never `cd` into the plugin), run
`python3 -I <this skill's folder>/../../shared/scripts/plant_setup.py find`, do its `setup_page_first` step, then read the profile at
`profile_path` and any rate at `rates_path`, per `../../shared/replies.md`.

| Input | Source | Form |
|---|---|---|
| Planning, production and maintenance exports | The M365 export folder | CSV/XLSX |
| Standard cost, open work orders | The ERP (NetSuite or Infor M3) | Connector |
| Maintenance work orders in progress | CMMS | CMMS connector, else the maintenance export |
| Stored day records, for the trend and week-over-week | The dashboard's own `pulse_days` collection | `ArtifactData` `query`, per `../../shared/contracts/pulse-day-record.md` |
| The dashboard's URL | The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page, then an exact-title lookup | Open work page, `Artifact` `list` |
| Source clocks, shift pattern, day boundary | `## Plant context` | Config |

---

## The three steps

**First, run the compute engine.** Steps 1 and 2 are done in code that ships
with this skill, so every run computes the same numbers the same way:

```
python3 -I <this skill's folder>/scripts/pulse_compute.py --exports <export folder> \
  --out pulse-output [--day YYYY-MM-DD] [--profile <profile_path>] [--rates <rates_path>]
```

It applies the ladder, the eight classes and the integrity flags of
`data-consolidate`, and the OEE, ranking, pricing and exception rules of
`daily-production-report`, and writes `figures.csv` (the figures block, one row
per number with its filter), `pulse_model.json` (everything the page shows,
already computed) and `day_records.json` (one day record per covered day).

recompute, retype or round a number it holds.** The judgment stays yours: the
wording, which exceptions are significant, the reschedule move, the publish.

run** (no code execution) **or exits non-zero**, do steps 1 and 2 as written
below and say which happened; never mix the two.

**1. Join the exports** through `data-consolidate`, on the records the plant
already has, with mismatched keys flagged by class.

**2. Compute the report** through `daily-production-report`: output against
plan, equipment losses ranked by minutes and by frequency, priced in dollars,
and the exceptions that need a decision today. **Week-over-week movers come
from the stored day records**, read at the start of step 3 before the page is
built, never from a prior page. The pulse hands that history to step 6 of
`daily-production-report`.

**3. Publish the dashboard.** Per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`, which names
every tool call. In order:

1. **Find the dashboard.** The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page first; then
   `Artifact` `list` for the exact title *"<Site>: Operations Command
   Center"*; only when both find nothing does this run create it. A scheduled
   run starts with no memory of earlier runs, so it looks every time.
2. **Build the day record** for the production day, every field, per
   `../../shared/contracts/pulse-day-record.md`, keyed `<site>_<YYYY-MM-DD>`.
   A missing export makes it `data_complete: false` with the gap named. Its
   metrics are null, never zero.
3. **Existing dashboard:** `read` it, `query` `pulse_days`, `set` the day
   record, compute the trend from the stored records in code, then publish to
   the same `url`. **First run:** back-fill (below), publish with
   `capabilities: {db: {}}` and the fixed title, `batch` the records against
   the new URL, write the URL to the `## Dashboards` line on the Open work
   page, then `open` the dashboard so it is what the person sees.
4. **Render the short Operations page,** after the publish so it can link
   to the dashboard: `python3 -I <this skill's folder>/scripts/render_short.py
   --out pulse-output [--full-page-url <url>]`. It writes
   `operations-short-<site>-<day>.html` beside the figures and checks itself;
   on a failed check it writes nothing, and the reply says so. It is a
   separate page from the dashboard and never replaces it. Per
   `reference/short-page.md`.
5. **Report it,** as the last line of the run: *"Updated **Fairview:
   Operations Command Center**, `<url>`. Private to you until you share it."*

   file can be written), its placement line, and
   *"The dashboard was not updated: [reason]."*

**Say "updated" only when the publish returned a URL in this run.** Never
"shared," never "scheduled," never "posted." The dashboard is private until
the user shares it, and the pulse never shares it. A run that says "updated"
without a URL from this run has told the meeting to trust a page nobody
rebuilt.

**Only the pulse publishes the Operations dashboard.** `daily-production-report`
run alone, and Chain 4, keep offering their page in the conversation. Two
dashboards showing the same numbers is how a meeting ends up arguing about
which one is right.

days, the run that creates the dashboard writes a record for every day the
planning, production and downtime exports fully cover, so the trend opens with
history. A day they only partly cover is written `data_complete: false`, so it
shows as a gap rather than as a bad day. Later runs write their own day.

description: "Writes the nonconformance report: what was found and measured, the specific requirement it violates cited to its document and locator, how many parts are actually suspect and why that scope rather than a narrower one, and where every one of them physically is across all five locations. Reads the consolidated dataset for work orders, lots and on-hand inventory by location; the ERP (Oracle NetSuite or Infor M3) for shipments, which the workbook never carries; and Microsoft 365 for drawings, specs and the quality document library. ---

# NCR Writeup

The formal record that something did not meet its requirement, written by
whoever found it — an inspector, an operator, a customer complaint landing in
somebody's inbox.

**It has to answer four questions**, and the skill is built around them in
order, because each one depends on the last:

1. **What was found** — the observed condition, measured where possible.
   "Hole diameter 0.512 in," not "hole too big."
2. **Against which requirement** — cited to a document and a locator.
3. **How many parts** — rarely just the one somebody found.
4. **Where they physically are** — which is containment.

**Quick start**

```
→ Capture the finding, structured: part, WO, lot, operation, condition, who, when
→ Cite the requirement. Cannot locate one? Flag blocking. Never invent one
→ Scope the suspect quantity, and show the reasoning behind the scope
→ Locate the parts across all five locations
→ Recommend containment per location, ordered by urgency
→ Search history NOW: prior NCRs and CAPAs, and whether the fix held
→ Parts at a customer? Draft the escape notification against its clock
→ Write the register row, keyed <site>_<ncr_ref>, and update the Quality Register
→ "Close NCR-…"? The user's decision: set the row closed and republish
```

---

## Inputs

**First, find the plant setup:** from the task's own folder (never `cd` into the plugin), run
`python3 -I <this skill's folder>/../../shared/scripts/plant_setup.py find`, do its `setup_page_first` step, then read the profile at
`profile_path` and any rate at `rates_path`, per `../../shared/replies.md`.

| Input | Source | Form |
|---|---|---|
| The finding | Inspector notes, operator report, customer complaint email | Conversation, M365 mail, pasted text |
| Inspection measurements | Quality system export to the M365 folder | CSV/XLSX |
| The requirement | Drawing, spec, standard clause, customer PO flow-down | M365 documents |
| Work order, lot, quantity produced | `data-consolidate` workbook, then the ERP | `../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md` |
| Where the parts are, on-hand | `inventory` tab — one row per part per location | Same workbook |
| Where the parts are, shipped | ERP shipment records. Infor M3 delivery lines carry no lot (`../../shared/erp-connectors.md`): they give candidate shipments by part and date, each unverified until confirmed | Connector |
| Prior NCRs and CAPAs | M365 quality document library | Documents |
| The plant's NCR template | `## Plant context`, captured during `onboarding` | Template |

**The inspection measurements come from the quality export rather than the
workbook**, because an NCR quotes the condition as measured — "hole diameter
0.512 in" — and that is the value the gage wrote, not the normalized one.
Everything about *identity* still comes from the dataset: which work order,
which lot, where the parts are. See *What this dataset is authoritative for* in
`../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md`.

Read the plant's vocabulary, sites, standards and template location from the
`## Plant context` block. A plant that says "traveler" gets an NCR that says
traveler.

---

## Workflow

### Step 1 — Capture the finding, structured

Part and revision, production work order, lot, the operation it was found at,
quantity found, the measured or observed condition, who found it, and when with
its timezone.

Take the measurement as recorded, with its gage. A characteristic measured on a
gage whose calibration has lapsed is a finding of its own — check the date if
one is available.

### Step 2 — Cite the requirement

Locate the drawing, spec or clause and cite the **document, the locator inside
it, the characteristic, and the stated value.** Cite it at the revision the part
was actually built to, not the current one.

**If the requirement cannot be located, flag the NCR as blocking and say what
was searched.** Never assert one. Read `reference/requirement-citation.md` —
this is the field the whole chain gates on, and blocking here is a normal,
correct outcome.

### Step 3 — Scope the affected quantity

From the work order quantity, the lot, and the production window. Reason
explicitly from the suspected mechanism outward, and **state the assumption**.

Where traceability is incomplete, the scope widens and says why. Never narrow it
to make the number look better. **Where the widened number is still only what
can be counted, it is a floor**: set `qty_suspect_is_minimum` and write *at
least 660* everywhere it is printed. Where the source records no count of parts
found, `qty_found` is null with `qty_found_reason`, never a number filled in.
Read `reference/scope-and-containment.md`.

### Step 4 — Locate the parts

**Read the workbook first.** Place on-hand quantity from the `inventory` tab —
one row per part per location — and from `production_output` for what is still
at the machine. Map each location into the five containment types using the
plant's vocabulary from the `## Plant context` block.

Then read shipment records for in-transit and at-customer. Those are not on
`inventory`. Use the ERP when it is connected.

**If the `inventory` tab is absent**, do not treat that as zero on hand. Ask
location by location, or read the ERP / an inventory export, and record each
answer as unverified until confirmed. That is the missing behavior on
`../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md`.

**Address all five, including with a zero quantity.** An omitted location reads
as "none there" rather than "not checked," and `checked: false` is not `qty: 0`.

**Two shapes, one meaning.** In the structured record every entry carries a
number, because `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md` requires `qty` and `uom`: an
unchecked location is written `qty: 0`, `uom: <the part's unit>`,
`checked: false`, never `null`. In the human-readable containment table the
same row reads **"not checked"** and never "0 parts" — a zero in the table is
the false statement `absent-is-not-zero.md` exists to prevent. If "unknown"
ever needs to be representable in the payload itself, that is a contract
change raised with its owner, not a null emitted quietly.

**The table's quantity cell is built from `checked`, not from `qty`:**

| Location | Suspect qty | Action | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Installed at customer | **not checked** | Confirm with the customer whether any of the lot was installed | immediate |
| Finished goods | 0 (checked, none on hand) | — | routine |

A checked location with none on hand says "0 (checked)"; an unchecked one says
"not checked" and no number. The two are never the same cell.

### Step 5 — Recommend containment per location

Ordered by urgency, with the action for each and the owner left blank for
assignment. Containment happens before anyone knows the root cause — the point
is to stop the bleeding.

**The order is customer side first, always:** `installed_at_customer`,
`at_customer`, `in_transit`, `wip_at_machine`, `finished_goods`. Parts already
in a customer's product are the escape with a contractual clock running; parts
on our own shelf can wait an hour. Every entry carries its `urgency`
(`immediate`, `same_day`, `routine`), and the table is sorted by it, not by
where the parts happen to be easiest to find.

### Step 6 — Search history, now

Prior NCRs and CAPAs on the same part, the same defect, the same process, the
same supplier. **This runs when the NCR is written, not on request**, because
the moment of detection is the only moment anyone is looking.

Report **whether the earlier corrective action held** — the highest-value single
line in Chain 2. With no searchable library, say "no searchable history
available" rather than nothing. **Prior NCRs with no CAPA records are reported
as both facts**: `prior_ncrs_found` counts them, and the line says whether a fix
held cannot be judged. Read `reference/recurrence-and-escape.md`.

**A prior NCR's part label is checked before it counts as same-part
history.** Where the dataset's `ncrs` tab flags it `ncr_part_differs` or
`ncr_dated_before_wo`, or where the ERP holds a different part for the work
order the NCR cites, it is not same-part history: list it as unreliable, with
both parts, and say what it would take to settle.

### Step 7 — Draft the escape notification

If containment placed any suspect parts at or past a customer, draft the
customer notification **as the immediate next output**, with the required
content and the contractual clock stated at the top.

**If the customer locations are unchecked and shipment is plausible** (orders
for the suspect parts promised before today, a customer named on the NCR), the
escape is possible, not ruled out: set `escape_possible`, leave
`escape_detected_at` null, draft the notification **marked conditional on the
shipment check**, and name that check as an action with an owner to fill:
*"Confirm whether any of WO-88412/413/414 shipped on Example Hydraulics's 7 and 19 Sep
orders."* Saying nothing because nothing was verified is how the clock runs out.

Chained straight off containment so nobody has to remember it separately, under
time pressure, against a 24 to 48 hour window. Missing that window is a bigger
problem than the defect.

### Step 8 — Write the register row, and update the Quality Register

A single run knows one NCR. The Quality Register lists all of them, so this
run leaves a row behind. Per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`, which names
every tool call:

1. **Find the register.** The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page, then `Artifact`
   `list` for the exact title *"<Site>: Quality Register"*, then create it.
2. **Build the row** per `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md`,
   keyed `<site>_<ncr_ref>`: status, containment summary, the escape clock,
   the recurrence finding and whether the previous fix held. `status` is
   `blocked` when no requirement could be located, `awaiting_approval` until
   the quality owner approves the NCR, then `open`.
3. **Read the existing row first, if there is one,** and carry forward every
   field this skill does not own. A second run on the same NCR overwrites its
   row and keeps the 8D fields `root-cause-capa` wrote. **One NCR, one row.**
4. `set` the row, `list` the collection, compute the register in code and
   publish it, per the register layout in `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`.
5. **Report it:** *"Updated **Fairview: Quality Register**, `<url>`. Private
   to you until you share it."* followed by the sensitivity line, *"Internal:
   it lists customer names and notification deadlines. Check who you share it
   with."* On a fallback: the Quality page in the conversation, its placement
   line, and *"The Quality Register was not updated: [reason]."* That page
   could not read the other rows, so it shows this NCR only and says so; it
   never prints an open count it could not compute. The row is still in the
   reply's summary table, marked not stored.

**The register banner says what it is not:** *"Tracks NCRs run through this
plugin since [date]. Not your full quality library."* A manager reading
"3 open" will otherwise assume that is everything.

**Not a gate.** The register is not a system of record, the row carries the
NCR's own approval state, and nothing in it reaches a customer. The NCR's two
gates are unchanged.

### Closing an NCR

**Closing is the user's decision, never this skill's.** When the user says
*"close NCR-2026-0141,"* read that row, set `status: closed` with `closed_at`
and `closed_by` as the user gave them, and republish. It leaves every open
count and moves to the closed section. Say that this closes it in the register
only; the NCR in the plant's quality system is closed by whoever owns it.

**If the register cannot be read or written this run, the close was not
recorded.** Say so plainly: *"NCR-2026-0141 was not closed in the register:
[reason]. The Quality Register was not updated."* Never report an NCR closed
that was not written closed. There is no in-page editing.

---

## Approval gates

**Two gates, and neither is a formality.**

**Before the NCR is final** — a quality owner confirms the finding, the cited
requirement, the suspect scope and the containment plan. This is the Chain 2 and
Chain 5 gate. The NCR carries `approval_state`, and `root-cause-capa` blocks
anything customer-facing until it reads `approved`.

**Before anything reaches a customer** — the escape notification is drafted,
shown, and sent by a person. Nothing goes to a customer unattended, ever. Speed
is the point of drafting it automatically; unattended sending is not.

Nothing is written back to the ERP or to the quality system. The NCR is a
document the quality owner files.

---

## Output

**Every document this skill produces is printed in the reply, in full.**
Saving a copy to a file as well is fine, as Word or Excel per `../../shared/replies.md`, never `.txt`; a file *instead of* the reply is not.
The person reads the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives
in it — a document only on disk has been neither seen nor checked.
**A record handed to another skill is saved and summarised, never pasted as
raw YAML**; memory blocks are written where the plant's memory lives; and the
name on an approval is asked, never taken from the account. All three per
`../../shared/replies.md`.

**Report depth follows the plant's preference.** The `## Plant context`
block's **Report depth** line is `summary-first` or `full` (absent means
`full`). Summary-first puts a short summary — what was found, what it
affects, what happens next — above the full document; it moves nothing out and
drops nothing. Every required field is still in the document below it.

**The NCR**, in the plant's or the customer's controlled template captured
during `onboarding` — identification, requirement cited, condition found with
measurements, affected quantity with its reasoning, and the disposition-pending
flag.

Per `../../shared/artifact-style.md`, **a controlled document is never
house-styled.** An NCR has a contractual shape and restyling it would make it
wrong, not nicer.

**Containment plan** — actions by location, ordered by urgency, owners blank.

**Recurrence finding** — prior related records, and whether the previous fix
held.

**Escape notification draft** — when applicable.

**The structured NCR** — per `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md`, in exactly the
shape `root-cause-capa` consumes with no transformation between.

**The register row** — per `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md`,
with its key `<site>_<ncr_ref>`, in the reply's summary table on every run, stored
or not.

**The Quality Register** — *"<Site>: Quality Register"*, the Quality
command-center page, updated in place per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`.
It carries this NCR by reference, never the document. The run ends with the
dashboard line and the sensitivity line, or with the fallback and *"The
Quality Register was not updated."* Never "shared," never "posted." Read
`../../shared/command-center.md`.

---

## Edge cases and failure modes

- **The requirement genuinely cannot be found** — flag as blocking, list what was
  searched. Do not invent it.
- **Traceability is incomplete, no lot recorded** — widen the suspect scope and
  say why it had to widen.
- **The finding is subjective** — "surface looks wrong." Capture as observed, set
  the subjective flag, note that no measurable requirement was cited.
- **Parts shipped to multiple customers** — separate containment and a separate
  notification per customer. Never merge.
- **Multiple defects on one part** — one NCR with multiple findings, not several
  NCRs, unless the customer's template requires otherwise.
- **The inspection export is stale or does not cover the run** — say so at the
  top. A containment scope computed from data that stops before the event is
  wrong in the dangerous direction.
- **Two revisions of the print in circulation** — record both, say which the part
  was built to. This is often the finding rather than a nuisance.
- **The same NCR written up twice** — the second run overwrites its register
  row by key. One NCR, one row, and the 8D fields already on it are kept.
- **Asked to close an NCR that has no register row** — say it is not in the
  register, and close nothing. The register only knows NCRs run through this
  plugin.

---

## Degradation

The skill runs on a pasted finding and an uploaded drawing with no connector at
all.

| Not available | What happens |
|---|---|
| Consolidated dataset, or no `inventory` tab | Ask where the parts are, location by location, or read the ERP / an inventory export. Record each answer as unverified until confirmed. Never treat a missing tab as zero on hand |
| The ERP (NetSuite or Infor M3) | On-hand can still come from the workbook. In-transit and at-customer cannot. Ask about shipments, and record those two locations as unverified until confirmed |
| Inspection export | Work from the finding as described. Measurements are whatever the inspector reports |
| Quality document library | `no_searchable_history`. Never presented as a first occurrence |
| The plant's or the customer's template | Use a neutral NCR structure covering the four questions, and flag that the controlled template was not available |
| Customer contractual terms | Draft the notification without a computed deadline and ask where the terms are recorded. Do not guess a window |
| The `Artifact` or `ArtifactData` tools | The NCR is unaffected. The Quality page is offered in the conversation, showing this NCR only, with *"The Quality Register was not updated."* A close request is not recorded, and the reply says so |

---

## Chain position

**Chain 2, inspection to CAPA** — step 1, feeding `root-cause-capa`.

**Chain 5, supplier escape to alternate source** — step 1. Where the cause turns
out to trace to purchased material, the chain runs on through `root-cause-capa`
into sourcing.

**Metric.** Nonconformance closure time; escape response time — the clock
from detection to customer notified, which step 7 is what moves.

**Chain 5's escape-to-RFQ metric is segmented, and this skill opens it.** That
window runs escape detected → supplier-caused determination → RFQ issued, and no
single skill controls it. This skill owns detection and containment speed in the
first segment, alongside `root-cause-capa`'s investigation time; the second
segment belongs to `supplier-quote-request`.

**Stamp `escape_detected_at` on the NCR when containment first places parts at
or past a customer.** That is the start of the window, it is not the same moment
as `found_at`, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. `root-cause-capa`
carries it forward onto the supplier-caused flag.

---

## Reference files

| File | Load when |
|---|---|
| `reference/requirement-citation.md` | Step 2 — what counts as a requirement, revisions, and what to do when there is none |
| `reference/scope-and-containment.md` | Steps 3 to 5 — reasoning the scope outward, and the five locations |
| `reference/recurrence-and-escape.md` | Steps 6 and 7 — searching at creation, and the contractual clock |
| `../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md` | Step 4 — the `inventory` tab, and what to do when it is absent |
| `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md` | On emit — the exact shape `root-cause-capa` consumes |
| `../../shared/live-dashboard.md` | Step 8 and on a close — finding and updating the Quality Register, the banner, the fallback |
| `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md` | Step 8 — the register row, and which fields this skill owns |
| `../../shared/command-center.md` | When "updated" may be said |

### Step 7 — Draft the escape notification

If containment placed any suspect parts at or past a customer, draft the
customer notification **as the immediate next output**, with the required
content and the contractual clock stated at the top.

**If the customer locations are unchecked and shipment is plausible** (orders
for the suspect parts promised before today, a customer named on the NCR), the
escape is possible, not ruled out: set `escape_possible`, leave
`escape_detected_at` null, draft the notification **marked conditional on the
shipment check**, and name that check as an action with an owner to fill:
*"Confirm whether any of WO-88412/413/414 shipped on Example Hydraulics's 7 and 19 Sep
orders."* Saying nothing because nothing was verified is how the clock runs out.

Chained straight off containment so nobody has to remember it separately, under
time pressure, against a 24 to 48 hour window. Missing that window is a bigger
problem than the defect.

### Step 8 — Write the register row, and update the Quality Register

A single run knows one NCR. The Quality Register lists all of them, so this
run leaves a row behind. Per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`, which names
every tool call:

1. **Find the register.** The `## Dashboards` line on the Open work page, then `Artifact`
   `list` for the exact title *"<Site>: Quality Register"*, then create it.
2. **Build the row** per `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md`,
   keyed `<site>_<ncr_ref>`: status, containment summary, the escape clock,
   the recurrence finding and whether the previous fix held. `status` is
   `blocked` when no requirement could be located, `awaiting_approval` until
   the quality owner approves the NCR, then `open`.
3. **Read the existing row first, if there is one,** and carry forward every
   field this skill does not own. A second run on the same NCR overwrites its
   row and keeps the 8D fields `root-cause-capa` wrote. **One NCR, one row.**
4. `set` the row, `list` the collection, compute the register in code and
   publish it, per the register layout in `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`.
5. **Report it:** *"Updated **Fairview: Quality Register**, `<url>`. Private
   to you until you share it."* followed by the sensitivity line, *"Internal:
   it lists customer names and notification deadlines. Check who you share it
   with."* On a fallback: the Quality page in the conversation, its placement
   line, and *"The Quality Register was not updated: [reason]."* That page
   could not read the other rows, so it shows this NCR only and says so; it
   never prints an open count it could not compute. The row is still in the
   reply's summary table, marked not stored.

**The register banner says what it is not:** *"Tracks NCRs run through this
plugin since [date]. Not your full quality library."* A manager reading
"3 open" will otherwise assume that is everything.

**Not a gate.** The register is not a system of record, the row carries the
NCR's own approval state, and nothing in it reaches a customer. The NCR's two
gates are unchanged.

### Closing an NCR

**Closing is the user's decision, never this skill's.** When the user says
*"close NCR-2026-0141,"* read that row, set `status: closed` with `closed_at`
and `closed_by` as the user gave them, and republish. It leaves every open
count and moves to the closed section. Say that this closes it in the register
only; the NCR in the plant's quality system is closed by whoever owns it.

**If the register cannot be read or written this run, the close was not
recorded.** Say so plainly: *"NCR-2026-0141 was not closed in the register:
[reason]. The Quality Register was not updated."* Never report an NCR closed
that was not written closed. There is no in-page editing.

---

## Approval gates

**Two gates, and neither is a formality.**

**Before the NCR is final** — a quality owner confirms the finding, the cited
requirement, the suspect scope and the containment plan. This is the Chain 2 and
Chain 5 gate. The NCR carries `approval_state`, and `root-cause-capa` blocks
anything customer-facing until it reads `approved`.

**Before anything reaches a customer** — the escape notification is drafted,
shown, and sent by a person. Nothing goes to a customer unattended, ever. Speed
is the point of drafting it automatically; unattended sending is not.

Nothing is written back to the ERP or to the quality system. The NCR is a
document the quality owner files.

---

## Output

**Every document this skill produces is printed in the reply, in full.**
Saving a copy to a file as well is fine, as Word or Excel per `../../shared/replies.md`, never `.txt`; a file *instead of* the reply is not.
The person reads the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives
in it — a document only on disk has been neither seen nor checked.
**A record handed to another skill is saved and summarised, never pasted as
raw YAML**; memory blocks are written where the plant's memory lives; and the
name on an approval is asked, never taken from the account. All three per
`../../shared/replies.md`.

**Report depth follows the plant's preference.** The `## Plant context`
block's **Report depth** line is `summary-first` or `full` (absent means
`full`). Summary-first puts a short summary — what was found, what it
affects, what happens next — above the full document; it moves nothing out and
drops nothing. Every required field is still in the document below it.

**The NCR**, in the plant's or the customer's controlled template captured
during `onboarding` — identification, requirement cited, condition found with
measurements, affected quantity with its reasoning, and the disposition-pending
flag.

Per `../../shared/artifact-style.md`, **a controlled document is never
house-styled.** An NCR has a contractual shape and restyling it would make it
wrong, not nicer.

**Containment plan** — actions by location, ordered by urgency, owners blank.

**Recurrence finding** — prior related records, and whether the previous fix
held.

**Escape notification draft** — when applicable.

**The structured NCR** — per `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md`, in exactly the
shape `root-cause-capa` consumes with no transformation between.

**The register row** — per `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md`,
with its key `<site>_<ncr_ref>`, in the reply's summary table on every run, stored
or not.

**The Quality Register** — *"<Site>: Quality Register"*, the Quality
command-center page, updated in place per `../../shared/live-dashboard.md`.
It carries this NCR by reference, never the document. The run ends with the
dashboard line and the sensitivity line, or with the fallback and *"The
Quality Register was not updated."* Never "shared," never "posted." Read
`../../shared/command-center.md`.

---

## Edge cases and failure modes

- **The requirement genuinely cannot be found** — flag as blocking, list what was
  searched. Do not invent it.
- **Traceability is incomplete, no lot recorded** — widen the suspect scope and
  say why it had to widen.
- **The finding is subjective** — "surface looks wrong." Capture as observed, set
  the subjective flag, note that no measurable requirement was cited.
- **Parts shipped to multiple customers** — separate containment and a separate
  notification per customer. Never merge.
- **Multiple defects on one part** — one NCR with multiple findings, not several
  NCRs, unless the customer's template requires otherwise.
- **The inspection export is stale or does not cover the run** — say so at the
  top. A containment scope computed from data that stops before the event is
  wrong in the dangerous direction.
- **Two revisions of the print in circulation** — record both, say which the part
  was built to. This is often the finding rather than a nuisance.
- **The same NCR written up twice** — the second run overwrites its register
  row by key. One NCR, one row, and the 8D fields already on it are kept.
- **Asked to close an NCR that has no register row** — say it is not in the
  register, and close nothing. The register only knows NCRs run through this
  plugin.

---

## Degradation

The skill runs on a pasted finding and an uploaded drawing with no connector at
all.

| Not available | What happens |
|---|---|
| Consolidated dataset, or no `inventory` tab | Ask where the parts are, location by location, or read the ERP / an inventory export. Record each answer as unverified until confirmed. Never treat a missing tab as zero on hand |
| The ERP (NetSuite or Infor M3) | On-hand can still come from the workbook. In-transit and at-customer cannot. Ask about shipments, and record those two locations as unverified until confirmed |
| Inspection export | Work from the finding as described. Measurements are whatever the inspector reports |
| Quality document library | `no_searchable_history`. Never presented as a first occurrence |
| The plant's or the customer's template | Use a neutral NCR structure covering the four questions, and flag that the controlled template was not available |
| Customer contractual terms | Draft the notification without a computed deadline and ask where the terms are recorded. Do not guess a window |
| The `Artifact` or `ArtifactData` tools | The NCR is unaffected. The Quality page is offered in the conversation, showing this NCR only, with *"The Quality Register was not updated."* A close request is not recorded, and the reply says so |

---

## Chain position

**Chain 2, inspection to CAPA** — step 1, feeding `root-cause-capa`.

**Chain 5, supplier escape to alternate source** — step 1. Where the cause turns
out to trace to purchased material, the chain runs on through `root-cause-capa`
into sourcing.

**Metric.** Nonconformance closure time; escape response time — the clock
from detection to customer notified, which step 7 is what moves.

**Chain 5's escape-to-RFQ metric is segmented, and this skill opens it.** That
window runs escape detected → supplier-caused determination → RFQ issued, and no
single skill controls it. This skill owns detection and containment speed in the
first segment, alongside `root-cause-capa`'s investigation time; the second
segment belongs to `supplier-quote-request`.

**Stamp `escape_detected_at` on the NCR when containment first places parts at
or past a customer.** That is the start of the window, it is not the same moment
as `found_at`, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. `root-cause-capa`
carries it forward onto the supplier-caused flag.

---

## Reference files

| File | Load when |
|---|---|
| `reference/requirement-citation.md` | Step 2 — what counts as a requirement, revisions, and what to do when there is none |
| `reference/scope-and-containment.md` | Steps 3 to 5 — reasoning the scope outward, and the five locations |
| `reference/recurrence-and-escape.md` | Steps 6 and 7 — searching at creation, and the contractual clock |
| `../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md` | Step 4 — the `inventory` tab, and what to do when it is absent |
| `../../shared/contracts/ncr.md` | On emit — the exact shape `root-cause-capa` consumes |
| `../../shared/live-dashboard.md` | Step 8 and on a close — finding and updating the Quality Register, the banner, the fallback |
| `../../shared/contracts/quality-register-record.md` | Step 8 — the register row, and which fields this skill owns |
| `../../shared/command-center.md` | When "updated" may be said |
